A.explanation: Wavelength $0.13 \text{ m}$ is about half the true wavelength, from counting a half-cycle as a full cycle.

B.explanation: Wavelength $0.13 \text{ m}$ is too small and then $f = v/\lambda$ gives about $30 \text{ Hz}$, double the correct frequency.

C.explanation: Three waves in $0.80 \text{ m}$ gives $\lambda \approx 0.27 \text{ m}$ and $f = 4.0/0.27 \approx 15 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: Wavelength $0.27 \text{ m}$ is correct but $30 \text{ Hz}$ does not satisfy $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

One wavelength $\lambda$ is the length of one full cycle, so divide the $0.80 \text{ m}$ length by the number of cycles you counted.
Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find $f$ from your value of $\lambda$.
walkthrough: The rope snapshot shows displacement against length from $0$ to $0.8 \text{ m}$, with speed $v = 4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right.
Count full repeats: there are three complete waves in the $0.80 \text{ m}$ section, with peaks near $0.07 \text{ m}$, $0.33 \text{ m}$ and $0.60 \text{ m}$.
Hence $3\lambda = 0.80 \text{ m}$, so $\lambda = 0.80/3 \approx 0.267 \text{ m}$, about $0.27 \text{ m}$.
For a progressive wave $v = f\lambda$, so $f = v/\lambda$.
Substitute with units: $f = 4.0/0.267 \approx 15 \text{ Hz}$, with unit $\text{s}^{-1}$ as expected for frequency.
Wavelength $0.27 \text{ m}$ with frequency $15 \text{ Hz}$ matches the table row. This is option C.
